previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and liver transplant was admitted with fever and right upper quadrant abdominal pain. Given her immunosuppressed state, she was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Imaging, including CT and MRCP, showed no evidence of infection, biliary obstruction, or appendicitis, though a stable soft tissue density near the abdomen was noted. Blood cultures and viral studies were negative, and autoimmune workup was unremarkable. Antibiotics were discontinued after 48 hours without recurrence of fever. She developed right lower quadrant pain during admission, which improved without surgical intervention. Her symptoms were attributed to post-transplant changes, possibly related to embolization coils or scar tissue. She was discharged home on tramadol and ondansetron for symptomatic management, with no changes to her baseline immunosuppressive regimen.

Discharge Instructions:
HOSPITAL SUMMARY
You were admitted to the hospital for evaluation of abdominal 
pain and abnormal labs on testing; more specifically, your white 
blood cell count was low, and there was concern that you had an 
active viral infection with CMV.  We treated your low blood 
count by giving you a medication called Neupogen, which 
increases the production of white blood cells by your body.  We 
think the low white blood cell level was caused by medication 
side effects, and we may changes to prevent this.  We initially 
gave you a antiviral medication for CMV, but subsequent testing 
showed that the initial CMV test was a false positive and that 
you actually do not have the infection.  For your abdominal 
pain, we performed a colonoscopy which did not show any 
abnormalities.  Biopsy was taken to rule out local infection.  
The results were pending at the time of your discharge, and your 
liver doctor ___ review them with you at your next visit.

medication for preventing a lung infection from dapsone to 
atovaquone.

review your colonoscopy biopsy results.

next time you should get a routine one for colon cancer
